verses.zh: 以色列出了埃及，雅各家离开说异言之民；
verses.en: When Israel left Egypt,when the family of Jacob left a foreign nation behind,[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 114. The psalmist recalls the events of the exodus and conquest and celebrates God’s kingship over his covenant people.
verses.commentary:
114:1-2 This Psalm is about the exodus from Egypt (cf. Exodus 1-12). The exodus is a direct fulfillment
of YHWH's revelation and promise to Abraham in Gen. 15:12-21. The exodus was the beginning of the People of God
as a nation (cf. Exodus 19-20).

Notice the different designations for the people of God.

- Israel

- house of Jacob

- Judah

114:1 "Israel" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name).

▣ "from a people of strange language" This phrase occurs only here in the OT. The AB (p. 134) takes the
same consonants and revocalizes them to fit the imagery of Isa. 25:3, where it denotes a "cruel people" (BDB 470, i.e.,
the Israelites' taskmasters, cf. Exod. 3:7). The same root is used with an emphatic lamedh (i.e., Hebrew letter L) in Lam. 4:3.

The historical reality of Israel's having to deal with foreign domination is recurrent (cf. Isa. 28:22; 33:19; Jer. 5:15).
The question of interpretation is how and why God's people were dominated by pagans (cf. Habakkuk). As God took the Canaanite
tribes out of the land because of their sin, so too, the Israelites because of their sin (i.e., the exiles by Assyria and Babylon).

verses.zh: 那时，犹大为主的圣所，以色列为他所治理的国度。
verses.en: Judah became his sanctuary,Israel his kingdom.
verses.commentary:
114:2 Because both Judah and Israel are mentioned, one wonders when this Psalm was written.

- the United Monarchy lasted from Saul ‒ Solomon

- in 922 B.C. the Kingdom split between

- Rehoboam in Judah

- Jeroboam I in Israel

- after the return from Persian exile under Cyrus II, the Israelites took their collective name again, although they
possessed only a small part of the tribal allocation of Judah (i.e., small area around Jerusalem)

verses.zh: 沧海看见就奔逃；约旦河也倒流。
verses.en: The sea looked and fled;[NOTE:1] the Jordan River[NOTE:2] turned back.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the house of Jacob from a nation speaking a foreign language.”
The psalmist recalls the crossing of the Red Sea (Exod 14:21).
Heb “the Jordan” (also in v. 5). The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
114:3-6 This is figurative language (cf. Ps. 18:7-15; 29:3-9; 68:7-8; 77:16-19). The two books that have helped me
most in the area of OT hyperbole and imagery are

- D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic

- G. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery of the Bible

It is significant that "water" is mentioned in several senses. Water is the only thing not specifically said
to be created in Genesis 1. Water in ANE mythology was divine (i.e., salt water, fresh water). There was conflict
between water and the gods. The Bible often uses this imagery to describe YHWH (cf. Job 41:1; Ps. 74:12-17; Isa. 27:1).
YHWH controls Leviathan in Job 3:8; Ps. 104:26. But also notice the "sea" is personified in Ps. 114:3,5 (along with other aspects of nature).

However, in Ps. 114:8 the life-giving aspect of water is stated. YHWH, not Ba'al, is the source of fertility (i.e., rain).

In a sense the imagery of separating water and dry land is an ANE allusion to initial creation. The goal of physical
creation was the creation of a people to fellowship with God (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8).

114:3 "The sea looked and fled" This could refer to

- the crossing of the "Red Sea" (lit. "sea of reeds," see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE RED SEA),
which is described in Exodus 14 and in Moses' poem in Exodus 15; God did it by using

- Moses' staff

- a strong east wind

- the crossing of the Jordan River at flood stage (cf. Joshua 3); see full exegetical notes on Joshua 3 online; God did
it by a landslide upriver, which began at just the right moment and ended at just the right moment

verses.zh: 大山踊跃，如公羊；小山跳舞，如羊羔。
verses.en: The mountains skipped like rams,the hills like lambs.[NOTE:1]
notes: The psalmist recalls the crossing of the Jordan River (Josh 3:13, 16).
verses.commentary:
114:4,6 The topological features of Canaan rejoice at the coming of YHWH and His people (cf. Ps. 96:9). This is
expressed in the Qal IMPERATIVE, "tremble" (BDB 296, KB 297), which denotes both

- trembling in fear (cf. 1 Chr. 16:30)

- dancing in joy (cf. Ps. 87:7; 96:9)

114:4 "The mountains" This could refer to Mt. Sinai, but probably to the "mountains" (i.e., hills) of Canaan.

verses.zh: 沧海啊，你为何奔逃？约旦哪，你为何倒流？
verses.en: Why do you flee, O sea?Why do you turn back, O Jordan River?

verses.zh: 大山哪，你为何踊跃，如公羊？小山哪，你为何跳舞，如羊羔？
verses.en: Why do you skip like rams, O mountains,like lambs, O hills?
verses.commentary:
114:6 Notice this verse repeats the VERB of Ps. 114:4.

- skip, Ps. 114:4 ‒ Qal PERFECT

- skip, Ps. 114:6 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT

Psalm 114:5-6 asks the question as to "why" nature acted so strangely. It was because of the presence
of the Creator. What happened at the inception of the people of God is meant to continue!

verses.zh: 大地啊，你因见主的面，就是雅各　神的面，便要震动。
verses.en: Tremble, O earth, before the Lord—before the God of Jacob,
verses.commentary:
114:7 The earth physically convulses at the approach of the Creator.

Notice He is called "Lord" (Adon) here, not "Lord" (YHWH),
as in Ps. 114:7a and Eloah in 114:7b.

verses.zh: 他叫磐石变为水池，叫坚石变为泉源。
verses.en: who turned a rock into a pool of water,a hard rock into springs of water.[NOTE:1]
notes: The mountains skipped like rams, the hills like lambs. This may recall the theophany at Sinai when the mountain shook before God’s presence (Exod 19:18).
verses.commentary:
114:8 The verse alludes to two specific occasions during the wilderness wandering period where YHWH
supernaturally provided life-giving water (cf. Ps. 78:15; 105:41).

- Exodus 17:6

- Numbers 20:11

It is used to describe the eschatological period in Isa. 48:21 (i.e., a second exodus).
